notes: Questions are phrased the way an engineer under pressure actually types them, not the
way someone who already knows the answer document would phrase them. The first draft of
this file was written the second way and naive retrieval scored 0.91 — which told us
nothing except that we had written the questions backwards.
difficulty records the doc-level rank naive retrieval gives the expected document, so a
regression tells you which band broke. match=all marks the multi-hop cases.
The ACL case is deliberately absent: it needs a visibility argument and is demonstrated

cases.question: checkout is throwing errors for customers and there is nothing in our logs
cases.exercises: vocabulary mismatch — the root-cause ADR never contains '502' or 'error'; it says pool saturation and upstream gateway timeout

cases.question: users cant place orders and our dashboards look fine
cases.exercises: symptom described from the wrong layer — three checkout documents rank above the one that explains it

cases.question: why is it 502ing?
cases.exercises: the query is not a search key — no service, no version, a pronoun subject

cases.question: who do I page for catalog
cases.exercises: every catalog-svc document outranks the platform policy that actually holds the answer

cases.question: the numbers dont match what the provider says
cases.exercises: the postmortem about the symptom outranks the ADR that defines the process

cases.question: which services still use the deprecated v3 auth flow, and who owns them?
cases.exercises: multi-hop — two independent tables, and the second lookup depends on the first

cases.question: how long before we give up delivering to a dead endpoint
cases.exercises: the gateway deadline ADR is a near-miss competitor for anything phrased as a timeout

cases.question: can I just update the amount on that entry
cases.exercises: the honest answer is 'you cannot' — retrieval must surface the append-only rule, not the reconciliation runbook

cases.question: partner says we sent the same event twice
cases.exercises: the postmortem about one incident outranks the ADR stating that duplicates are guaranteed

cases.question: do we still need to call auth on every request
cases.exercises: superseded conflict — the v3 API reference ranks first and answers 'yes', which is now wrong

cases.question: what does an empty upstream_status mean
cases.exercises: the naming-convention ADR that merely reserves the field outranks the one that defines its meaning

cases.question: how do I know if search is behind
cases.exercises: the runtime signal is one field in an API reference, surrounded by documents about the same subject

cases.question: can a partner turn off deliveries permanently
cases.exercises: the answer is a single status code in a table; three notify documents outrank it

cases.question: when am I allowed to skip the wait during key rotation
cases.exercises: the postmortem about skipping the wait outranks the runbook that says when it is permitted

cases.question: why is the same order showing twice in fulfilment
cases.exercises: two plausible causes in two services — idempotency keys or at-least-once delivery

cases.question: should the incremental indexer be stopped while a full reindex runs
cases.exercises: yes/no question whose answer is a warning inside step 4 of a runbook

cases.question: what python version do we target
cases.exercises: one-shot lookup — the routing baseline; anything beyond a single search is wasted latency

cases.question: is it safe to bump the timeout on that route
cases.exercises: the answer is an explicit 'do not' at the end of a runbook

cases.question: i rotated the db password and now nothing can connect
cases.exercises: strong lexical and semantic overlap — the case naive retrieval is good at

cases.question: everything is down and its not any single service
cases.exercises: symptom-shaped question that maps cleanly onto one postmortem

cases.question: why did every service start returning 401 at once
cases.exercises: distinctive symptom, single owning document

cases.question: do we ever delete money records
cases.exercises: a question with a false premise — the retention table says ledger entries are never deleted

cases.question: what happens to rate limiting if redis is down
cases.exercises: a deliberate trade-off the assistant must report as designed, not as a bug

cases.question: is the broker thing decided yet
cases.exercises: the answering document is a draft — the assistant must say so rather than report it as decided

cases.question: how do I roll back a checkout deploy
cases.exercises: superseded conflict — the 2025 blue/green runbook has a near-identical title and ranks in the top 5
